predecessors.name: Taifa of Dénia
predecessors.text: the Balearic Islands, Dénia's since 1015 and autonomous under the governor Abd Allah ibn Aglab from 1050

successors.name: Almohad Caliphate
successors.text: the Balearic Islands, where the Almohads 'installed their own governors' after executing Abdallah ibn Ishaq in 1203

rulers.name: Muhammad I ibn Ali ibn Yusuf (Banu Ghaniya)

ledger.x: 1076: the Balearic Islands become the independent Taifa of Majorca under Ibn Aglab al-Murtada.
August 1114: the Pisan-Catalan fleet holds Ibiza and invests Palma.
1115: 'In 1115 they were reconquered by the Almoravids of peninsular Iberia.'
April 1115: 'the city capitulated and its entire population was enslaved'; the Crusaders left within months and the taifa ruler was taken to Pisa.
1147: after the Almoravids fall at Marrakesh the islands become independent: 'A new, independent kingdom arose, the second taifa (1147-1203), under the Banu Ghaniya dynasty.'
1185: 'In his absence, the Almohads retook the islands in 1185' while Ali ibn Ishaq was campaigning in the eastern Maghreb; Muhammad ibn Ishaq was reinstalled under Almohad suzerainty.
By 1187: Abdallah ibn Ishaq 'recaptured the islands from the Almohads by 1187'; the page gives no year or method, so the year is the latest it allows.
1203: Abdallah is 'defeated and executed by the Almohads in 1203, who installed their own governors on the islands after this'.
1203: the Taifa of Majorca ends; 'Almohads: 1203-1229' in the succession list, then the Crown of Aragon.

wars.name: 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition
wars.outcome: A Christian victory: the city of Majorca capitulated in April 1115, but the Crusaders held the islands only a few months and the Almoravids reconquered them in 1115.

wars.name: Almohad reconquests of the Balearic Islands
wars.outcome: The Almohads retook the islands in 1185, lost them again by 1187 to Abdallah ibn Ishaq and took them for good in 1203.

certainty.note: The coast bounds the realm, but the pages never say which islands were held (Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera are not named on the Taifa or Banu Ghaniya pages); the Balearic Islands region is the reading.
